The blocking at live_academy.rs:623-626 is per workflow, so a failed W65 checkpoint with a successful start still allows a later W53 exam.start or W66 progress.resetCourse in the same family before the hand-off. Consider blocking every non-cleanup mutation while daily_unsettled is true, or requiring W65 calls to sort contiguously.

The default mutation cleanup text 'synthetic coursework on a test account (owner-designated)' (live_academy.rs:721-724) is also written for exam.start and progress.resetCourse. That misdescribes a timed exam attempt that is not retired, and a destructive reset. The follow-up says to record how the disposable attempt is retired or expires. unsettled_call marks needs-reconciliation for any Err from call(), including desk.json() and admission refusals that happen before dispatch (live_run.rs:777). It also writes 'a dispatched mutation ... may remain'. This is safe because it errs toward reconciling, but it is broader than the documented 'admitted mutation that exceeds the core settle bound'. Consider telling admission/pre-dispatch errors apart from settle timeouts.

The manifest template says 'state-changing procedures must claim their corresponding interactive workflow'. Only exam.start, progress.resetCourse and shift.start/serve/answer/decide are mapped (contracts.rs:40-51). Other mutations, such as exam.submit, enrollment.removeByCourse and units.complete, are gated only by permitted_operations, the account pin and an explicit expectation. Narrow the wording, or add mapped contracts for other destructive mutations.

Attempt-05 R1 is closed. mutation_found (live_academy.rs:375-385) stops with reconcile=true for any outcome=unknown, of kind error or failed. That matches the core mapping: Failed/Error carry the settlement outcome, and confirm-after-PUT and any non-Data reply are Unknown (learner_domain.rs:604-621, 1074-1100, 1174-1180). A Core Err after a mutation (settle timeout in Desk::academy, live_run.rs:783-785) settles a needs-reconciliation receipt through unsettled_call and breaks the loop; it no longer propagates Err. Ctx::settle never downgrades a reconcile stop. A reconcile stop skips the later families, the avatar, L14 and sign-out. The new fixture applies the remote effect before a Close/Hang. Avatar policy confirmed: an upload Err or unknown result returns before removal and requires reconciliation. A rejected or not-sent upload returns without removal and without a stop. After a confirmed upload, a removal that is Err, unknown or rejected is needs-reconciliation. Both calls are charged before either is sent.

Confirmed again in the current source: case-folded unique labels limited to 1-96 [A-Za-z0-9_-], checked before any dispatch, with receipt ids that cannot collide with fixed ids. Backward-only references with type preserved, rejecting malformed pointers or reference objects. Explicit expectations are mandatory, and inline grading needs an exact boolean verdict. DSL separators fail closed. Missing or malformed SuperJSON fails. Critical procedures are mapped to their workflows, with duplicate caps and ordered mandatory assertion sets for W53/W65/W66. The W66 reset compares the baseline with positive progress, matches all four cleared counts, reads back zeros and compares the whole certificate array with a non-empty baseline. Checkpoints require every planned call to validate and no failed call in the row. A non-cleanup mutation is blocked after a failed checkpoint of the same workflow. Dependencies are not ready, or a budget is refused, before anything is charged or sent. Daily marker semantics are as recorded. Mutations require a pinned lowercase-hex expected_account_sha256 that must match the signed-in identity before any program or avatar call. Receipts redact answer/values and summarize private literals, and the sign-in receipt drops call.* inputs.
